lead.headline: Poochinski survives the comeback by 5.12
lead.dek: Maye I touch your TDs? walked into Sunday night leading the 6-2 team. Bucky Irving went for 28.5. It wasn’t enough: Caleb Williams and Luther Burden III answered, and every starter in the matchup is final at 181.76 to 176.64.
lead.pull: Poochinski 181.76, Maye I touch your TDs? 176.64. Final whistle, nobody left.
body: I’ve covered Poochinski all season, and this is the first time I’ve watched it get chased. It went into Sunday night trailing the 2-6 team, with two players left against one. It came out with 181.76, the top score on the board this week, and a 5.12-point escape.

The night game was a three-man shootout. Maye I touch your TDs? got everything it could have asked for from Bucky Irving: 28.5 against a 17.51 projection. Poochinski had more bullets. Luther Burden III, a flex call that was Questionable this week, scored 20.7. Caleb Williams added 16.76. That was the comeback, erased one stadium at a time.

The call that saved this team was made before kickoff. Poochinski started Chris Olave over Chris Godwin Jr. at receiver. Olave scored 16.8. Godwin scored 4.8 on the bench. In a 5.12-point game, that’s the whole margin and then some. CeeDee Lamb’s 33.5 and Javonte Williams’ 22.4 did the heavy lifting; the lineup decision kept the lights on.

Now the cruel part, from the other side of the field. Maye I touch your TDs? scored 176.64, the third-highest score in the league this week, and lost. Brock Purdy 26.28, Drake Maye 21.26, Christian Watson 30.1, Irving 28.5. Breece Hall scored 11.7 on its bench while Tyler Allgeier scored 6.6 in the lineup. Swap them and it still loses, by two hundredths of a point. That isn’t a lineup mistake. That’s a curse.

Poochinski banks the win and pulls level with AB81, the 7-1 team that lost today. The Insider’s read for next week: Jahmyr Gibbs scored 13.4 against a 25.69 projection and Sam LaPorta 7.2. A team that just won by 5.12 can’t keep surviving on Lamb and lineup luck.

quick_hits.headline: Big Stric Energy’s week is one Monday game
quick_hits.body: Bad things man bad things leads 156.56 to 100.18, and the whole matchup now rides on Buffalo at Minnesota, Monday at 5:15 PM Pacific. Big Stric Energy has Josh Allen (22.01 projected) and Justin Jefferson (17.59); Bad things has Allen’s teammate James Cook III (14.9). Allen and Jefferson have to outscore Cook by the full gap, and they’re projected for 39.6 together. The live projection is 171.46 to 139.78, and the odds say 3.3%. Playoff odds: 29.1%.

quick_hits.headline: The 1-7 team won with a zero at quarterback
quick_hits.body: Santa Clara’s Finest started Lamar Jackson, on IR, in a two-quarterback league and still beat deeboliciouskins 140.04 to 117.64. Joe Burrow went for 29.54, Kenneth Walker III 36.3, and the kicker Spencer Shrader 16.0. Sunday night didn’t change it: Colston Loveland’s 9.4 beat D’Andre Swift’s 3.1.

quick_hits.headline: deeboliciouskins lost with a 0.0 at receiver
quick_hits.body: George Pickens was Out and started anyway, so deeboliciouskins played a man down and lost by 22.4. Ja’Marr Chase’s 31.5 couldn’t carry it alone, and Swift at 3.1 against a 19.25 projection sealed it. Whether the empty slot cost the game is Monday’s question: DJ Moore, 12.78 projected, sits on the bench and plays tomorrow. He’d need more than 22.4 to make this hurt.

quick_hits.headline: Cherry Blossom’s 178.18 lands second
quick_hits.body: Cherry Blossom beat AB81 178.18 to 120.56 on Puka Nacua’s 35.0, and for most of Sunday that was the week’s top score. Poochinski’s 181.76 passed it tonight. AB81, the 7-1 team, takes its second loss.

quick_hits.headline: Bad things got away with 36.36 on the bench
quick_hits.body: C.J. Stroud scored 36.36 on the Bad things bench while Malik Willis scored 4.82 at quarterback. It won’t matter unless Monday turns historic. The Chicago defense added 15.0 tonight and Bad things sits at 156.56 with Cook still to play.

w9-m1.headline: Allen and Jefferson have to outrun Cook
w9-m1.blurb: Bad things man bad things 156.56, Big Stric Energy 100.18, everything else final. Monday at 5:15 PM Pacific: Josh Allen and Justin Jefferson, 39.6 projected together, against James Cook III, 14.9. Live projection 171.46 to 139.78. Bad things, 96.7%.

w9-m2.headline: Final: Santa Clara’s Finest 140.04, deeboliciouskins 117.64
w9-m2.blurb: Two busted lineups, one winner. The Finest played without a second quarterback and won by 22.4; deeboliciouskins played without a receiver and didn’t.

w9-m3.headline: Final: Poochinski 181.76, Maye I touch your TDs? 176.64
w9-m3.blurb: Bucky Irving’s 28.5 against Caleb Williams’ 16.76 and Luther Burden III’s 20.7 on Sunday night. The favorite escapes by 5.12.

w9-m4.headline: Final: Cherry Blossom 178.18, AB81 120.56
w9-m4.blurb: Puka Nacua’s 35.0 led the way, and the 7-1 team takes its second loss.

w9-r2-s4.headline: Poochinski’s WR call won the game
w9-r2-s4.blurb: Chris Olave over Chris Godwin Jr. Olave scored 16.8, Godwin 4.8 on the bench. Poochinski won by 5.12. Do the math and send the front office a fruit basket.

w9-r7-s6.headline: The Finest’s TE call: Loveland, 9.4
w9-r7-s6.blurb: Colston Loveland took the spot over Hunter Henry and scored 9.4 on Sunday night. Henry scored 6.5 on the bench. Small win, real win.

w9-r7-s4.headline: The Finest’s WR call: Boston, 15.8
w9-r7-s4.blurb: Garrett Wilson was Out. Denzel Boston, projected for 10.75, took the spot and scored 15.8 in a game the Finest won.

w9-r6-s6.headline: deeboliciouskins’ TE call: Warren, 8.4
w9-r6-s6.blurb: Tyler Warren started over T.J. Hockenson and scored 8.4. Hockenson plays Monday from the bench, after the matchup is already decided.

alert_notes.6: George Pickens started at receiver while Out. The slot finished at 0.0 and deeboliciouskins lost 140.04 to 117.64. DJ Moore, on the bench, plays Monday.
alert_notes.7: Lamar Jackson started at quarterback from IR. The 0.0 stood all weekend, and Santa Clara’s Finest won 140.04 to 117.64 anyway.

external_facts.claim: Tampa Bay at Chicago on Sunday night is final; Buffalo at Minnesota is Monday, Mon 5:15 PM Pacific.
